title: Repository licensing: PolyForm Noncommercial and AI-training reservation

completion_criteria.text: Establish the actual licensing state of the repo and what third parties may and may not do with it
Choose a license satisfying attribution and noncommercial restriction, with the open-source trade-off made explicitly
Add LICENSE and NOTICE carrying the PolyForm terms, the TDM reservation, and the kickstart.nvim MIT carve-out
Express the AI-training reservation in machine-readable form (robots.txt, ai.txt, tdmrep.json)
Remove the false MIT claim from README and declare the license in package.json
Open a PR to main and drive all CI checks green
Merge the PR to main so the license is in effect on the default branch
Diagnose the nondeterministic secret-scan CI failure rather than accepting a re-run as the fix
Replace gitleaks-action with a pinned, checksum-verified direct binary invocation so the api.github.com dependency is unreachable, keeping the gate red on real findings

spine.active_goal: The license and the machine-readable reservation are in effect on main; what remains is deciding whether to mirror to an owned domain, the step that actually activates the EU reservation.
spine.next_step: Settle the disposition first: all nine criteria are met, but the active goal's mirror half is untouched, so either close this thread and open a successor scoped to the mirror, or reopen it with a mirror criterion. Then take the mirror on real numbers - domain, host, sync mechanism, cost. Needing a human: both merged branches still exist locally and on the remote, and vcs_ref names the stale one. Filed, unrelated: task_9ce31094.
spine.last_session: Merged PR #62, putting the license in effect on main, then diagnosed the secret-scan flake to its root cause and shipped PR #63 replacing gitleaks-action with a pinned checksum-verified binary. Both merges verified against origin/main; the new gate is green on both CI paths on real runners.

open_risks.text: re-verify branch-local facts after any checkout — this session asserted a CI gate that exists only on an unmerged branch and nearly shipped an orphan receipt, because a file read is only true of the tree it came from
do not present the machine-readable opt-out files as active protection while the repo is GitHub-hosted — crawlers fetch github.com/robots.txt rather than the repository's copy

do not treat CI as a full-history secret gate — it scans only the pushed commit range, and the one real credential found sits at .config/github-copilot/apps.json kept out of the repo by gitignore alone

do not collapse the three-arm gitleaks fallback into a single tip-only scan — a tip-only scan was demonstrated exiting zero on a secret committed earlier in the same push, so the gate went green on a real leak

key_decisions.title: Trade the OSI open-source label for the noncommercial restriction
Express the AI-training refusal in machine-readable form, not license prose alone
Invoke the gitleaks binary directly rather than the Action wrapper
Keep the secret scan diff-scoped, and prefer a bounded full scan over a silent green

out_of_scope: Formal copyright registration or obtaining legal counsel - this work is a factual read of the repository's licensing state and the options available, not legal advice.

Relicensing the kickstart.nvim-derived material under .config/nvim/ - that upstream MIT grant runs directly from its own authors and cannot be revoked or narrowed from this repository; .config/nvim/LICENSE.md must stay in place.
Changing the terms that apply to forks taken before this change - the relicense governs forward only.
